key_insight: PanPep’s meta-learning framework retains predictive performance and transfers to independent peptide–TCR datasets when evaluated with robust negative-sampling strategies, demonstrating reusability beyond original training conditions.
problem_solved: Addresses poor generalization and uncertain reusability of peptide–TCR binding predictors by testing model robustness across independent datasets and realistic negative-sampling schemes.
method: Apply PanPep (meta-learning-based peptide–TCR binder predictor) to extended, independent evaluation datasets not used in original training.
Compare multiple negative-sampling strategies and evaluation protocols to measure performance sensitivity and potential evaluation bias.
Perform controlled ablations and cross-dataset transfer tests to quantify reusability and robustness of learned representations.
impact: Provides a reproducible evaluation blueprint for biosequence ML models, showing meta-learning can improve cross-dataset transfer — important for practitioners building models intended for real-world, out-of-distribution biological applications.
visual_elements: Schematic of PanPep meta-learning workflow (support/query tasks, fast adaptation) with TCR and peptide inputs
Bar chart or grouped bars showing performance metrics across original vs independent datasets and different negative-sampling strategies
ROC/PR curves or confusion matrices comparing evaluation protocols to highlight evaluation bias
Flow diagram of the reproducibility/evaluation pipeline (data splits, negative sampling, ablation steps)
paper_title: Reusability report: Meta-learning for antigen-specific T cell receptor binder identification
paper_authors: Fei He, Xianyu Wang, Dong Xu
